lesson.name: Learn The Alekhine's Defense
lesson.description: Learn the main lines and key ideas in the Alekhine's Defense for both Black and White.

{What can White play to spark a strong attack?} 6. Nxf7 {[%wrong There's a
stronger option. Try to find a good capture.] [%hint Sacrifice to draw out the

{How should Black fight against the imposing white pawn center?} 5... dxe5 {
[%wrong There's a better move. Try to find a good capture.] [%hint Trade off
one of White's center pawns.]} (5... Bf5 $5 {This is playable, but there's a
more popular option. Try to find a good capture.}) (5... c5 $2 6. dxc5 {
White is doing well. Try to find a strong capture.}) (5... g6 $5 {This is
reasonable, but there's a more popular option. What is that move?}) (5... g5 $2
6. Nc3 {This risky line should be better for White with correct play. Try to
find a safer move.}) 6. fxe5 {Good start! How should you develop another piece?
} Nc6 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try to find a good developing move.] 
[%hint Develop and attack d4. ]} (6... Bf5 $5 {This is a good move, but
there's another strong idea that develops with a threat. Try to find it.}) (
6... c5 $5 7. d5 {This is playable, but it's safer to develop. How should you
do that?}) (6... e6 $2 7. Nc3 {Black's position is too passive. Try to find a
strong developing move.}) 7. Be3 {Good work! What's the best square for your
c8-bishop?} Bf5 {[%wrong White is doing well. Try to find a better developing
move.] [%hint Develop your c8-bishop to control the center.]} 8. Nc3 {Nice
move! How should you prepare to develop the f8 bishop?} e6 {[%wrong There's a
better move. Try to find a way to allow your f8-bishop to develop.] [%hint
Prepare to play Be7 and castle.] Well played! All of Black's minor pieces will
find active squares.} (8... Nb4 $2 9. Rc1 {White can easily defend the fork.
Try to find a strong developing move.}) (8... g6 $2 9. Nf3 {White's center is
too powerful. Try to find a pawn move to give you some central control.}) *

white center pawns immediately. How can you do that?}) 11. O-O {Nice move! How
should you secure your king?} O-O {[%wrong There's a better move. Try to find
a way to secure your king.] [%hint Castle before the f-file opens.]} (11...
fxe5 $2 12. d5 {White has a strong initiative. Try to find a safer move.}) 12.
exf6 {Well played! How should you recapture?} Bxf6 {[%wrong There's a better

(12... Rxf6 $2 13. Nh4 {White has a strong initiative. Try to find a better
capture.}) (12... gxf6 $2 13. Kh1 {Black's exposed king gives White an edge.
Try again and look for a more precise capture.}) *

better move. Try to find it.}) *

{White has sacrificed a pawn for an initiative. How should you develop with a
threat?} 8. Qg4 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for
a strong threat.] [%hint Develop your queen to attack an undefended pawn.]} (8.
Nf3 $2 d5 {Black counterattacks in the center with a good position. Try again
and look for a stronger threat.}) (8. b4 $2 Qh4 {Black targets f2 and c4 with
good position. Try again and look for a stronger threat.}) (8. Qf3 $2 Qh4 {
Black targets c4 and f2 with a good position. Try again and look for a more
useful queen move.}) 8... O-O {Black would have been better off defending with
Kf8 or Bf8. How should White continue the attack?} 9. Bh6 {[%wrong There's a
better option. Try again and look for a strong threat.] [%hint Develop and
threaten checkmate.] Great job! The best Black can do is g6, which loses an
exchange. White may even prefer to continue the attack with moves like Nf3 and
h4 instead of capturing on f8!} (9. Bg5 $5 {This is a good choice, but it's
best to threaten immediate checkmate. How can you do that?}) *

{How did GM Ivanchuk finish off his brilliant game against Magnus Carlsen?} 37.
Qxe8+ {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look for a stronger
attacking move.] [%hint Sacrifice your queen and then prepare to promote a
pawn.]} (37. cxb6 $5 {This is a good move, but GM Ivanchuk preferred to
sacrifice his queen before capturing a pawn. How did he do it?}) (37. Qf4 $5 {
White is doing well, but Black has dangerous counterplay. Try again and check
the hint if you're stuck.}) (37. Qd3 $2 bxc5 {White is doing well, but Black
has dangerous counterplay. Try again and check the hint if you're stuck.}) (37.
Qd2 $2 bxc5 {White is doing well, but Black has dangerous counterplay. Try
again and check the hint if you're stuck.}) 37... Kxe8 {Great move! How should
White justify the queen sacrifice?} 38. cxb6 {[%wrong There's a better move.
Try again and look for a way to create a dangerous passed pawn.] [%hint
Prepare to promote your c-pawn.] Great job! Black has no way to stop the
passed b6-pawn. White soon won in Ivanchuk - Carlsen, 2007.} (38. Ra8+ $2 Ke7 {
After cxb6 and f5-f4, Black should be able to force a perpetual check. Try
again and look for a stronger move.}) *
